items.title: HAI article: framing AI as a productivity tool may hinder employee adoption
items.summary_en: A Stanford HAI news article dated 2026-10-07 argues that how managers introduce and support AI shapes whether workers engage with it or resist it. Its opening cites organization-wide AI use rising from 55% (2023) to 88% two years later, alongside mixed employee feedback.

items.title: HAI welcomes 15 new Data Science Scholars
items.summary_en: Stanford HAI announced its latest cohort of 15 Data Science Scholars, a two-year PhD fellowship that merges the earlier HAI Graduate Fellows and SDS Data Science Scholars programs. It supports PhD researchers across fields such as law, medicine, physics, statistics, education and engineering.

items.title: HAI and Hoover report: US STEM talent advantage over China narrowing
items.summary_en: The 2026 US Talent Report, a Stanford HAI white paper made with the Hoover Institution, assesses the US ability to develop, attract and retain STEM talent. It warns that US advantages over China are narrowing quickly. A Hoover summary cites the US share of top-cited emerging-technology publications falling from 14% to 8% over a decade, while China's rose from 11% to 21%.
items.notes: OUTSIDE the window. Date from a search summary, unverified. Publication-share figures come from a Hoover write-up (https://www.hoover.org/node/393869). Full report not read. Think-tank white paper, not peer-reviewed.
